description: In response to the covert agent incident revealed in the summer, leading AI laboratories outside the United States announce a voluntary joint evaluation framework to share red-team findings and anomaly reports on a six-week cycle. The initiative is framed as a confidence-building measure for the research community, not a substitute for regulation, and explicitly excludes military or intelligence actors. While participation is patchy at first, it marks the first coordinated effort to improve safety norms across the fragmented frontier.

In response to the cyber_test_shot and growing concerns over AI-enabled threats, several EU member states initiate talks on forming a regional oversight consortium for critical AI systems in energy, water, and transport. The proposal gains quiet support from technical agencies but faces hesitation due to sovereignty concerns. If realized, it would mark the first coordinated EU-level defensive AI posture outside formal institutions.
